entries.title: Senate rejects cloture on the motion to proceed to H.R. 3633, the digital asset market structure bill, 49-50
entries.facts: On September 15, 2026 at 02:19 PM the U.S. Senate took Roll Call Vote No. 234 of the 119th Congress, 2nd Session on the question "On Cloture on the Motion to Proceed (Motion to Invoke Cloture: Motion to Proceed to H.R. 3633)." The Senate's record states the result as "Cloture on the Motion to Proceed Rejected," with 49 Yeas, 50 Nays and 1 Senator not voting, and records the required majority as "3/5." The Senate's record states the measure title as "To provide for a system of regulation of the offer and sale of digital commodities by the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, to amend the Federal Reserve Act to prohibit the Federal reserve banks from offering certain products or services directly to an individual, to prohibit the use of central bank digital currency for monetary policy, and for other purposes."
entries.source_label: U.S. Senate — Roll Call Vote No. 234, 119th Congress 2nd Session, 09/15/2026 (H.R. 3633)
entries.relevant_to: digital asset exchanges, crypto trading platforms, broker-dealers, derivatives venues, stablecoin issuers

entries.title: New York Attorney General leads an 18-jurisdiction bipartisan coalition of attorneys general urging Senate leaders to preserve state enforcement authority in the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act
entries.facts: On September 14, 2026 New York Attorney General Letitia James announced that she led a bipartisan coalition of 18 attorneys general in a letter to Senate leaders on the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act. The announcement states that the attorneys general warn the legislation would "jeopardize their ability to protect investors from rampant digital cryptocurrency fraud," and objects to a grant of authority allowing the Securities and Exchange Commission to preempt state registration authorities. Per the announcement, the letter asks Congress to preserve states' enforcement role for both tokenized and non-tokenized securities, to maintain state registration regimes requiring crypto platforms to certify with states, to preserve federal-state cooperation, and to clarify ambiguous language. The announcement lists the joining jurisdictions as Arizona, California, Connecticut, Delaware, Illinois, Kansas, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, Nevada, New Jersey, Ohio, Virginia, Washington, Wisconsin and the District of Columbia.
entries.source_label: New York State Office of the Attorney General — press release, 09/14/2026
entries.relevant_to: crypto trading platforms, digital asset issuers, state-registered money transmitters, exchanges operating under state registration regimes
